source.title: Temporal Reversal Regularization for Spiking Neural Networks: Hybrid Spatio-Temporal Invariance for Generalization
source.authors: Lin Zuo; Yong-Qi Ding; Wenwei Luo; Meng-Meng Jing; Kun-Shan Yang

record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates temporal reversal regularization for spiking neural networks, but does not test any of the eight claim versions. Its results report test accuracy and spike firing rates, not training-to-test gaps or the interventions and measures specified in those versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results for its own temporal reversal and feature hybridization method. These results are recorded under fits_no_version; cited comparisons and theoretical bounds are not experimental rows.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates temporal reversal and feature hybridization in spiking neural networks. Neither these interventions nor its firing-rate measurements test V1–V8. Using SGD or Adam on different tasks does not compare optimizers, and its PAC-Bayesian argument does not test magnitude-aware weight sharpness.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors' main conclusion: temporal reversal and feature hybridization improve SNN generalization across static, neuromorphic, and point-cloud tasks. The authors additionally claim a tighter PAC-Bayesian generalization bound and improved adversarial robustness. Combined TRR improves the reported ablations, but feature hybridization alone reduces Transformer accuracy on CIFAR10 and CIFAR100.
record.recipe_differences: Adds temporal reversal consistency and firing-rate feature hybridization during spiking-network training; this is not a test of the claim versions' interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and architecture; feature reversal location; balance coefficient α, whose effect is most significant for DVS-Gesture; the paper reports that later reversal locations yield smaller gains. The Spike-driven Transformer feature-hybridization-only condition degrades CIFAR10/100 performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Combined TRR improves baseline accuracy across the recorded architectures and datasets. These are results for a different regularization intervention.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Temporal reversal plus firing-rate feature hybridization can improve held-out accuracy in the tested spiking neural networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Later reversal locations yield smaller accuracy gains; temporal reversal outperforms random temporal shuffling in both neuromorphic datasets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The benefit of TRR depends on the location and form of temporal perturbation.

fits_no_version.finding: NDA before TRR gives 78.20/92.48 accuracy; replacing reversal with NDA gives 78.77/94.33 on CIFAR10-DVS/DVS-Gesture, versus TRR's 77.60/91.67.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Combining or replacing temporal reversal with neuromorphic augmentation can further improve the tested TRR recipe.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 6 reports lower firing rates after TRR at all four displayed stages.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: TRR can reduce spike firing rates in the tested VGG-9 network.

fits_no_version.finding: Firing-rate hybridization exceeds binary-spike hybridization on both displayed datasets, subject to Table 13's inconsistent CIFAR10-DVS baseline.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Firing-rate hybridization can outperform direct binary-spike hybridization.

record.problems: No training-to-test gaps are reported. Main ablation tables give test accuracy but no uncertainty estimates; the ImageNet and adversarial experiments are single-trial results. Table 6's flattened layout makes some method-to-value assignments unclear.
record.rows_left_out: Comparative benchmark tables largely compare TRR against other methods and are not extracted as rows. Table 6 method/value mappings are unclear in the supplied flattened text, so only unambiguous values were retained; cited prior-work results were not recorded as this study's results.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting versus natural-label held-out performance under matched architectures and recipes.
Width sweeps beyond zero training error and subsequent test-error changes.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Matched optimizer comparisons and effects of tuning, decoupled weight decay, or switching optimizers.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size dependence, and joint dropout/weight-decay removal.
Magnitude-aware weight sharpness, its correlation with generalization gaps, and comparisons with other measures.
Removing highly memorized training examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8; this does not negate the reported TRR accuracy gains. Appendix B.2 says results average three runs except ImageNet and adversarial experiments, which use single trials; dispersion estimates are not reported. The citation to Exploring Generalization in Deep Learning supplies a PAC-Bayesian bound rather than a test of V7.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and their effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and effects of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and effects of tuning, weight decay, or optimizer switching.
Large versus small batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout effects and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with the train-test gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.
